c.tagline: Laid-back Sichuan capital of pandas, teahouses, and mouth-numbing hotpot.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥8-9; most residents book via Didi, and drivers overwhelmingly expect Alipay or WeChat Pay rather than cash.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police, 120 for ambulance, and 119 for fire; English-language support is limited, so having a translation app or local help ready is useful.

hood_landmark.Jinjiang / Chunxi Road: Sino-Ocean Taikoo Li Chunxi Road, Chengdu
hood_landmark.Qingyang / Kuanzhai Alley: Kuanzhai Alley (Wide and Narrow Alleys), Chengdu

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in crowded Chunxi Road and metro stations, and decline overly friendly invitations to teahouses or bars that can end in inflated bills.

hood_desc: Central downtown core around the Chunxi Road pedestrian street and the open-air Sino-Ocean Taikoo Li mall; best for first-timers who want shopping, food, and metro links all within walking distance.
The historic heart with the Qing-era Kuanzhai Alley (Wide and Narrow Alleys), the Qingyang Palace Taoist temple, and People's Park teahouses; best for old-Chengdu atmosphere and sightseeing.
Home to the Wuhou Shrine (Three Kingdoms memorial), the reconstructed Jinli Ancient Street, and a lively Tibetan quarter; best for culture, street snacks, and evening strolls.
Chengdu's modern high-tech and financial district of skyscrapers, the New Century Global Center, and Jiaozi Park; suits business travelers and those wanting new malls and calmer, newer surroundings.
A practical transit-hub district around Chengdu North Railway Station with wholesale markets and inexpensive hotels; convenient for onward high-speed rail and budget stays.
lodging: Ji Hotel Chengdu Gaoxin Financial Center
Home Inn Chengdu North Railway Station
7 Days Inn Chengdu North Railway Station

water.note: Tap water meets basic standards but isn't recommended to drink untreated; stick to bottled water.

transit.hours: Metro trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; buses run from early morning to around 10-11 PM, with Didi and taxis covering later hours.
transit.note: Chengdu Metro is one of China's largest systems, with 17+ lines topping 720 km, backed by an extensive bus network and a tram line in the outer districts.
transit.pay: Fares start at ¥2 by distance; pay with the Tianfutong transit card, a QR code via the Tianfutong or Alipay app, or single-ride tickets from station machines. Cash is rarely used.

bus: Intercity coaches from Chadianzi, Beimen, and Xinnanmen bus stations

car.idp: Not recognized (a temporary or full Chinese driving license is required)

train: Chengdu East, Chengdu South & Chengdu North railway stations (high-speed rail to Chongqing, Xi'an, Kunming and beyond)

transit.m: Metro Line 10 from Shuangliu Airport to the center (~30 min, transfer to Line 3/1)
Airport shuttle buses to key downtown points; note the newer Chengdu Tianfu Int'l (TFU), ~50 km SE, handles most long-haul flights and links by Metro Line 18 / airport rail

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Chengdu; restaurant bills are paid as-is and rounding up is neither required nor common.
